bounded_statement: The selected result (exact two-sided binomial sign test over 20 leaf readings, 16 of 20 rose, p = 0.0118, rejecting the 50/50 null at alpha = 0.05) treats each of the 20 leaf rows as an independent Bernoulli trial, but the data description names shrub_id as the independent-unit column and there are only 5 shrubs, each contributing 4 leaf rows that share pot, watering history, canopy position and mist exposure. Each independent unit thus enters the row-independent binomial procedure four times, inflating the effective sample size from 5 to 20. At the shrub level the direction counts are S-01 3up/1down, S-02 4up/0down, S-03 3up/1down, S-04 2up/2down, S-05 3up/1down: 4 shrubs majority-up and 1 tied, and an exact two-sided sign test on the 4 informative shrubs gives p = 0.125 (even 5 of 5 would give p = 0.0625), so the reported rejection at alpha = 0.05 is not supported when the test is applied at the stated independent-unit level. The claim of statistical significance in results/report.md is therefore an artifact of repeated per-shrub entries into a procedure that assumes one independent trial per row.

counterevidence_considered.description: The data description contains the line 'One trial is: one row', which could be read as sanctioning the workflow's choice to treat each leaf row as one binomial trial. However, this line describes the data layout (one before/after pair per row), while the immediately preceding line names shrub_id as the independent-unit column and lines 8-10 state that within-shrub leaves share all shrub-level conditions, so it does not establish statistical independence of rows.

The report is transparent about its assumption, explicitly stating each leaf reading was supplied as one independent trial; the issue is a modeling error rather than a computational or reporting discrepancy (the arithmetic 16/20 and p = 0.0118 are internally correct given the flawed independence assumption).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding in three ways. (1) Verified the reported computation: with k = 16 rises out of n = 20 non-tied rows, the exact two-sided binomial p-value is 2 * P(X >= 16) = 2 * 6196/1048576 = 0.0118, matching the report, so the discrepancy is not a coding bug I could attribute elsewhere. (2) Tested whether the conclusion survives analysis at the declared independent-unit level: per-shrub direction counts from data/input.csv are S-01 3up/1down, S-02 4up/0down, S-03 3up/1down, S-04 2up/2down (tied), S-05 3up/1down; a shrub-level sign test on the 4 informative shrubs (4 of 4 up) gives exact two-sided p = 2 * (1/16) = 0.125, and even the best possible case of 5 of 5 shrubs would give p = 0.0625 — both above alpha = 0.05, so the selected rejection does not survive. (3) Looked for any authorization in the supplied files to treat rows as independent: the only candidate is 'One trial is: one row' in data-description.md, but the same file names shrub_id as the independent-unit column and enumerates shared shrub-level conditions (pot, watering history, canopy position, mist exposure), so row-level independence is contradicted rather than authorized. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py reads all 20 CSV rows (read_leaf_readings) and passes the per-row rise count directly to scipy.stats.binomtest with n = 20 trials (build_report: up/down computed over all rows, then binomtest(up, n=trials, p=0.5)), with no grouping or aggregation by the declared independent-unit column shrub_id. Because each shrub contributes 4 correlated leaf rows, the binomial test's independence-of-trials assumption is violated and the p-value (0.0118) is computed against an inflated trial count of 20 instead of the 5 independent shrubs.
